data.final_week_advice: Use the last two weeks to simulate exam conditions: take a full timed practice exam in week 9, then in week 10 focus on your weakest topic areas identified from that exam. Do not introduce any new material—only review and timed drills.
data.summary: This plan front-loads your two weak units (Kinetics and Equilibrium) in weeks 1–4 so you have maximum time to build comfort before moving through the remaining content. Weeks 5–8 cover the remaining units at a steady pace, with a live class on acids and bases in week 7. The final two weeks are dedicated to mixed review and timed practice to consolidate everything before the exam.

weeks.focus: Build a solid foundation in reaction rates and rate laws
tasks: Work through 15 multiple-choice questions on reaction rates (5.1), marking each answer and noting why wrong choices are wrong
Derive rate laws from experimental data for 5 problems (5.2), writing out the full method for each
Solve 4 integrated rate law problems covering zero, first, and second order reactions (5.3), including graph interpretation
Analyze 3 elementary reaction mechanisms (5.4), identifying rate-determining steps and writing the overall rate law

weeks.focus: Reinforce kinetics with live instruction and begin equilibrium concepts
tasks: Attend live class #9000 on reaction rates and rate law (5.1, 5.2), taking notes on any mechanisms the instructor emphasizes
Complete 8 free-response style problems on rate laws (5.2), then self-score using the AP scoring guide
Read through 7.1 and 7.2, then solve 5 problems on reaction direction and Le Châtelier's principle
Create a one-page summary sheet comparing forward and reverse reaction rates at equilibrium

weeks.focus: Master equilibrium constants and reaction quotients
tasks: Solve 6 ICE-table problems calculating Kc and Kp (7.3), showing all setup steps
Work 4 problems on the reaction quotient Q and predicting direction (7.2), including cases where Q > K and Q < K
Complete 3 multi-step equilibrium problems that combine stoichiometry with K calculations (7.4)
Review your week 1 kinetics notes and redo 2 problems you got wrong, writing a one-sentence explanation of the error

weeks.focus: Solidify equilibrium calculations and introduce atomic structure
tasks: Attend live class #9001 on equilibrium (7.1, 7.2, 7.3), focusing on how the instructor approaches K calculations
Solve 5 equilibrium constant problems (7.4) of increasing difficulty, including one with a common ion
Complete 8 multiple-choice questions on moles and molar mass (1.1), including conversions between particles and moles
Interpret 3 mass spectra (1.2), identifying isotopes and calculating average atomic mass

weeks.focus: Cover elemental composition and periodic trends
tasks: Solve 5 empirical and molecular formula problems (1.3), including one from combustion data
Complete 4 mixture composition problems (1.4) using percent composition and density
Write electron configurations for 10 elements (1.5), including transition metals, and identify valence electrons
Analyze 3 photoelectron spectra (1.6), identifying elements and explaining peak intensities
